The accessories and upgrades are one of the best parts of the platform, really makes it a whole different experience from typical gun ownership where you've maybe only got a couple options. You should enjoy this springtime in your AR15 life and buy all the accessories you want to try, because parts are very interchangeable (rail mount especially) and before you know it, you'll have about enough spare hardware for a second AR.. then a third..

I will say though that fancy charging handles and bipods on ARs are very common overkill accessories. You can spend a fucking hundred dollars on some premium charging handle with a brand name, and really all it will do is stick out further from your rifle and increase the chance you might catch it on something. Aftermarket charging handles, like Raptors, are just fucking enormous and 5x as expensive as they should be. You should be able to release a standard charging handle with the tip of one finger, but people put these giant walrus paddles on there. See how far you get with a standard one before, in my opinion, wasting money on something that makes your rifle less solid and stable. Bipods are also kind of overkill for an AR, they're most useful on a rifle you'll be laying down with, and .223/5.56 isn't really that rifle. They can be fun for sitting down and plinking but don't train like that. Really it might just add weight to the front of your rifle and get in the way of your grip. UTG makes some decent cheap bipods in the $30 range.

Big upgrades will be a good optic and possibly a nice trigger which can make a marginal difference. I've had good luck with mid-grade optics like Ade or UTG.

Time to get a second and time to start training and learning the nuances of both, so get to practicing field service. When Marines are at the Rifle Range, they fire 50-60 rounds a day at three different distances. We didn't put all of that in one or two mags, the average was 5 rounds as that forced a mag change. Oh, learn your mags. Just because they claim to be able to hold whatever amount you are allowed, doesn't mean it will work properly. We were issued six 30 round magazines and if you filled them to capacity, you were guaranteed to have a problem.

You can never have enough mags, and you'll never have enough ammo. You'll also need ways to carry the mags so you can change mags and not fumble around in a bag like the lady at the supermarket digging through her purse.

Get some spare parts, and figure out how to change all of them. Bicyclists have an equation: N+1>1 and it means you should have more than 1, you wouldn't want your 1 to be in pieces and not functional when you need it.

Practice practice practice. You can get all the gadgets you want but the only thing that matters is the gunfag behind the trigger. A good shooter can put lead in target with iron sights and an out of the box firearm.
